claimant_lives_in_uk.description: Whether the claimant lives in the UK.

children.description: A list of children the claimant is claiming for.

lives_with_claimant.description: Whether the child lives with the claimant.

in_approved_education.description: Whether the child is in approved education or training (e.g. A-levels, GCSEs, NVQ up to level 3). Only relevant for children aged 16-19.

in_extension_period.description: Whether the child (aged 16 or 17) has left education and registered with a government-sponsored careers service or the armed forces (qualifying for a 20-week extension).

upkeep_per_week.description: The amount in £ per week the claimant contributes towards the child's upkeep (food, clothes, pocket money, etc.). Only relevant if the child does not live with the claimant.

another_claimant_has_priority.description: Whether another person who also lives with the child has priority for claiming Child Benefit.

another_claimant_lives_with_child.description: Whether someone who lives with the child is already claiming Child Benefit for them.

care_weeks.description: The number of weeks the child has been in local authority care.

care_home_24h_per_week.description: Whether the child spends at least 24 hours per week at home while in local authority care.

hospital_weeks.description: The number of weeks the child has been in hospital or residential accommodation.

claimant_spends_on_child.description: Whether the claimant regularly spends money on the child (e.g. food, clothes, books) while the child is in hospital or residential accommodation.

is_fostered.description: Whether the child is fostered by the claimant.

council_pays_for_child.description: Whether the local council pays towards the child's accommodation or maintenance.

works_24_plus_hours.description: Whether the child works 24 or more hours per week in paid employment.

started_apprenticeship_in_england.description: Whether the child has started an apprenticeship in England.

receives_qualifying_benefits.description: Whether the child receives qualifying benefits in their own right, such as Universal Credit or Employment and Support Allowance.

conversation.text:
Hello! I'd be happy to help you determine if you're eligible for Child Benefit.

To assess your eligibility, I'll need to ask you some questions. Let me start with the basics:

**Do you have any children you're responsible for, and if so, how many children are you asking about?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Hi, yes, I'm asking about my son Alex. He's 8 years old and lives at home with me.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for that information. I can see you're asking about your son Alex, who is 8 years old and lives at home with you.

To assess your eligibility for Child Benefit for Alex, I need to ask a few more questions:

**Where do you live? Specifically, do you live in the UK?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Yes, I live in the UK.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Great, thank you. Now I need to understand a bit more about your situation:

**Are you the person responsible for Alex's care? In other words, do you provide for his needs such as food, clothes, and pocket money?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Yes, I am. I provide for all his needs - food, clothes, everything he needs.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Excellent. Just a few more questions to complete the assessment:

**Is Alex currently in hospital, in care, or in any residential accommodation, or does he live with you full-time at home?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Well, he's been in care for a couple of months now, but he comes home to stay with me on the weekends and during the week too - so he does spend quite a bit of time at home with me.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for sharing that information. This is an important detail that affects eligibility. Let me ask for some clarification:

**How many hours per week does Alex spend at home with you? Is it at least 24 hours a week or more?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Yes, it's at least 24 hours a week. He stays with me on weekends and some evenings during the week.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for providing all that information. Let me assess Alex's eligibility for Child Benefit based on what you've told me.

You've confirmed that:
- Alex is 8 years old
- He lives with you in the UK
- You are responsible for his care and provide for all his needs
- He has been in care for a couple of months
- He spends at least 24 hours a week at home with you

According to the Child Benefit rules, when a child goes into care for more than 8 weeks, you would normally no longer be entitled to Child Benefit. **However, there is an important exception:** if the child spends at least 24 hours a week at home, you can continue to receive Child Benefit.

Since Alex spends at least 24 hours per week at home with you, this exception applies to your situation.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
**Good news! You are ELIGIBLE for Child Benefit for Alex.**

Even though Alex has been in care for more than 8 weeks, you meet the exception to the rule because he spends at least 24 hours per week at home with you. Since you're responsible for his care, provide for his needs, and he's under 16, you qualify for Child Benefit.

If you haven't already claimed, you can apply for Child Benefit. If you're already receiving it and were worried about Alex being in care, you should continue to be eligible as long as he maintains at least 24 hours per week at home with you.

Is there anything else you'd like to know about Child Benefit?
